answer: Press **Shift-Enter**. It opens or creates the page exactly matching what you typed, whereas **Enter** opens the selected (closest) match.

## When I type a new page name in the picker it keeps opening the closest existing match. Which key makes it open or create exactly what I typed?

--- [vault:corpus/docs/Guide/Find and Connect Pages.md] ---
### Create the linked page

# Create the linked page
On `Photo Walk`, click `Woodland Hike`. A link can name a page before it even exists (although it will appear in orangy-red). Following the link opens that page so we can start writing it.

You can also open the page picker, type `Woodland Hike` and notice that it’s already in the list _even though it does not exist_. This is what’s called an [[Aspiring Pages|Aspiring Page]]: it’s a page that does _not yet_ exist, but is already linked to. It’s _aspiring_ to become a real page one day. Today is that day.

On `Woodland Hike`, enter the following content:

```markdown
Sam Rivera is planning a woodland hike on 2026-06-21.

# Plan
* Follow the woodland trail.
* Bring the camera from our [[Photo Walk]].
```

We now have two outing pages, with a link in each direction.

--- [vault:corpus/docs/Guide/My First Markdown Page.md] ---
### Creating a page

# Creating a page
In your space, press **Cmd-k** on macOS or **Ctrl-k** on Windows/Linux to open the [[Page Picker]] (or click the book icon in the top navigation bar).

The Page Picker serves two purposes:
1. Navigating to _existing_ pages
2. Creating _new_ pages

While unusual to mix these activities, it has a purpose: [[Discovery]]. It is quite common that we want to create pages about topics we’ve already created pages for _before, but we’ve forgotten_.

Using the page picker to create new pages, this “rediscovery” tends to happen organically, as those pages (may) resurface as you type in the name of your new page.

In the page picker input box type `Photo Walk`, then press **Shift-Enter** to create a page with exactly that name. If your space already contains other pages that match “photo walk” in their name, they may appear here too and hitting **Enter** would open that old page rather than create a new page, pressing **Shift-Enter** ensures you create a new page.

It’s time to start typing. Enter the following markdown (or copy and paste it):

```markdown
Sam Rivera is planning a photo walk on 2026-06-14.

# Plan
* Meet at the riverside path at 08:00.

# Pack
* [ ] Charge camera battery
* [ ] Pack binoculars
* [x] Check the weather

Next weekend, let’s go on a [[Woodland Hike]].
```

### Create topic pages

# Create topic pages
Start with subjects you want to return to. In the [[Page Picker]] (**Cmd-k / Ctrl-k**), type a title and press **Shift-Enter** to open that exact name. Write enough context that the page makes sense when opened directly.

Keep each page focused enough that its name is useful in a sentence. You can start at the top level and add folders later. [[Guide/Best Practices]] describes the tradeoffs.

### Untitled

Use the page picker to find a note by name or create one in a writable space. For searching inside notes, use [[Search]]. The published documentation is read-only: use your own space for the creation steps below.

The page picker has two main functions:

1. Enables quick navigation between [[Page]]
2. Enables creation of new pages
   * Based on the entered name
   * Based on [[Link|linked]] to, but not yet created page names

The page picker can be invoked by clicking the 📔 icon in the top bar, or by pressing `Cmd-k` on Mac, or `Ctrl-k` on Windows/Linux.

The main input is the **filter phrase** and can be used to narrow down the list of page results.

If the filter phrase contains `#tags` the results will be filtered based on matching those tags.

If the filter phrase starts with `$`, the picker switches to navigating [[Markdown/Anchor|anchors]] instead of pages: everything after the `$` filters anchor names from across your [[Space]], and each result shows a snippet of the anchored content along with the host page it lives on. Deleting the `$` returns you to the page list. This works from any of the pickers.

> **note** Note
> Any page tagged with a tag starting with `#meta`, even though technically regular pages, will **not** appear in the page picker. To navigate to them, use the [[Meta Picker]] instead.

Pressing the `Enter` key will open/create the selected page.

### Using a panel

# Using a panel
* `Up` / `Down` (or `Ctrl-p` / `Ctrl-n`) move the selection, `PageUp` / `PageDown` by five, `Home` / `End` to the ends.
* `Enter` opens the selected row. `Escape` closes the panel, whether or not you have typed anything.
* Typing ranks rows fuzzily, highlighting the matched characters in each row’s name, list or tree alike.
* In a tree, `Right` expands (or steps into) a folder and `Left` collapses it (or steps out to its parent). `Enter` on a plain folder expands it, on a folder that is *also* a page it opens the page.
* `Tab` / `Shift-Tab` step through the segments in lists and trees. In tables they move keyboard focus between controls. Use `Ctrl-Left` / `Ctrl-Right` in the filter input to switch segments.
* `Shift-Enter` creates whatever you typed, in views that allow it. A create row also appears on its own: second in a list, pinned below the tree in a tree.
* The **first character typed into an empty box can route**:
  * `^` narrows the page picker to [[Meta Page|meta pages]].
  * `$` opens the anchor picker
  * `#` the tag picker
* In the page picker, `Space` on an empty phrase inserts the folder you are currently in, and `Alt-Space` extends the phrase by one more path segment of the best match. A `#tag` anywhere in the phrase filters by tag rather than matching names.

In a tree that supports it: drag a row onto a folder to move it (renaming through SilverBullet’s own machinery, so backlinks follow).
